title: Check a Round Trip Without Losing Data

blocks.text: Recovering Objects Does Not Require Recovering Every Character

We can read a sample, write its objects, and read that text again. The recovered data must preserve the groups that are present, including empty groups, each record's ID, its quantities, and the order of both vectors. Recovering the same number of groups or the same sum of accepted quantities is not enough.

Our writer chooses one textual representation: exact names, specific spaces, and integers without a plus sign or leading zeros. The input might have used different amounts of whitespace and +07 for ID 7. We therefore do not require the input text and composed text to be identical. We require equal data and, afterward, a stable composed representation.

blocks.question: Two sets each contain a record 7[2;1], but one associates it with red and the other with blue. Are they the same data under this contract?
options: Yes, because the record's ID and quantities match.
Yes, if both have one group and one record.
No: its association with the group must also be preserved.
blocks.explanation: The group is part of the complete identity. Counting or adding totals would hide that change.

blocks.text: Define a Comparison That Detects Data Loss

Define mismos_datos for valid sets: compare the number of groups; then, at each position, the group ID and number of records; finally, the ID and both quantities of each record at the same position. Return false if either set is invalid. Here, order is part of the contract, although other formats might choose to ignore it.

blocks.question: One set contains an empty red group and a blue group with one record; the other contains only blue with that record. Their totals match. What should the comparison return?
options: false, because a group that was present disappeared.
true, because an empty group contributes no quantities.
true if the remaining record has zero quantities.
blocks.explanation: Presence cannot be reconstructed from quantities or totals.

blocks.text: Check bounds before traversing. The comparison may convert already bounded sizes to int: there are at most three groups and ten records per group, so conversion preserves the value. Checking equal sizes before at() lets us use the same indices in both collections.

blocks.question: Both sets contain the same two records in red, but their vectors store the records in opposite order. What should this comparison do?
options: Ignore order because the writer always sorts.
Return false because the contract preserves order.
Return true only when their quantities match.
blocks.explanation: The writer traverses vectors without sorting. Changing their order changes something we agreed to preserve.

blocks.text: Implement the comparison and build the test: prepare a valid original Conjunto; compose its text; read it into another Conjunto; compare the original with the recovered one; compose a second time and compare the two composed strings. Check each bool before proceeding so you can distinguish a composition error from a reading error.

Use blue with 7[0;0], followed by red with 4[3;1]. Predict the bool values and the composed text. Then create variants of the recovered objects by changing only the group, only one quantity, only an ID, and only the order. Each change must be detectable; do not test only report totals. Keep the comparison variants valid: change to an unused ID, another available group, or a quantity in 0..10. If you introduce only invalid data, false might demonstrate domain validation rather than a difference in the tested field. Test invalid data too, but as a separate goal.
The reference appears after your attempt. The earlier readers and composer are provided as support; you construct the equality criteria and the sequence of checks.

The first line is 1:1:1. The second is { set { group blue 7[0;0] } { group red 4[3;1] } }. We preserve order, valid zero, and associations. Textual stability only supplements the data comparison; it does not replace it.

Criteria: check each stage, compare every identity and quantity at its position, distinguish an empty but present group from an absent group, and keep original and recovered data independent. Also complete the variants that must differ, along with an empty-set case.

blocks.question: Predict both lines. The conversions used by this text are valid for our reader.
blocks.explanation: The reader obtains the data, and the composer writes them in the chosen form. Whitespace, plus signs, and leading zeros from the input are not copied literally.

blocks.text: A Stable Representation May Still Be Incomplete

blocks.question: This counterexample composes incompleto instead of original. Predict the two bool values.
blocks.explanation: Both composed strings match, but the empty, present red group is missing. Stability alone does not demonstrate preservation.

blocks.text: A test that always reads the output of a writer that drops data may produce stable text. The starting point must therefore be the complete original, with comparison independent of report totals. Check empty groups, zero-valued records, multiple groups containing the same local ID, and different orderings.

Transfer: next convert one group's records to the presence table studied earlier. That table does not preserve arrival order. If you change the organization, explicitly decide which equality matters and preserve another representation when the original order must be recoverable. Do not silently change the contract to make the test pass.

Representations and reading structures are covered in the primary source (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 9.9.1–9.9.3, pp. 270–275); the exercise revisits its reading and writing examples. The criteria, comparison, and experiments are original to this learning path.
